property_summary: When calling transfer with an array of three addresses, the reference contract transfers tokens to all three addresses while the buggy contract skips the first address, resulting in different token balances for address[0].

Calling transfer with an address array of length 1 and checking that the reference contract makes an external call (causing a revert when the target address does not support transferFrom) while the buggy contract skips the loop because i=1 >= _tos.length and thus makes no call, so the assertion on the revert boolean differs.

When _tos array contains two addresses, the reference contract calls transferFrom on both addresses, while the buggy contract (starting loop at i=1) skips the first address; the assertion checks that after the call, the external contract's totalCalls state variable equals 2 for reference and 1 for buggy.
